note: Brand and domain routes, each seeded from a measured run. A row is added by a benchmark, never by an opinion. Override order is property > domain > brand > default.

default.why: the lane that reached 21 of 30 properties across six buckets in pilot-002

MARRIOTT.why: 5/5 fetched, 100% precision and 100% critical recall across three pilots

HILTON.why: 3/3 fetched at 100% recall once the brand container was made to COMPETE with the generic walk instead of pre-empting it

IHG.why: 5/5 of the Milwaukee IHG cohort acquired at publication grade on a single Firecrawl attempt each, identity confirmed and a property-specific policy surface located on every one, measured with no fallback available. Five distinct extractions across five properties, no brand-generic text and no capture landing off the property page. This matters more here than elsewhere: IHG carries no petsAllowed in its JSON-LD, so the policy only arrives if the page paints it -- and it did, on all five.
IHG.max_attempts_rationale: 3, matching CHOICE and WYNDHAM. No IHG property needed more than 1, so this is headroom rather than a measured requirement.
IHG.known_reader_limitation: the provider is not the constraint on this lane; the READER is. Two of five sources state a weight limit that policy_reading does not extract, and one (Staybridge Milwaukee Airport South) has a TIERED fee reduced to its first tier. That is provider-independent -- the same text through any lane produces the same record -- and it is why the incumbent's own recall here was 62%. Records flagged by the tiered-fee audit are HELD from publication.

previous.note: 4/5 fetched at 62% recall and $2.71 for five properties -- the weakest and most expensive lane in the table. Unlike CHOICE and WYNDHAM, this demotion replaces a lane that was underperforming, not one that was working.

WYNDHAM.why: 7/7 of the remaining Milwaukee Wyndham properties acquired at publication grade on a single Firecrawl attempt each, with identity confirmed and a located policy surface on every one, measured with no fallback available so nothing could be credited to the incumbent. Five distinct policies across seven properties -- including two Super 8s that disagree with each other -- confirm the lane reads each page rather than returning a brand constant. The Web Unlocker stays as fallback because nothing here tested it and nothing here retires it.
WYNDHAM.max_attempts_rationale: 3, matching the CHOICE lane. No Wyndham property needed more than 1 in the decision test, so this is headroom rather than a measured requirement.

previous.note: the Browser API lane worked -- 5/5 at 100% recall -- and is not being retired for failing. It is being demoted because a cheaper lane matched it, and it is now FORBIDDEN on this route only to keep the ladder from silently re-entering an expensive provider on a technical failure. That is a cost decision, and it is reversible.

CHOICE.why: Firecrawl acquired 15/15 of the Milwaukee Choice queue against the Web Unlocker's 7/15 over the same rows -- including four the Unlocker returned ACCESS_DENIED on -- at 30.6s against a measured 130.0s, with zero structured mismatches over the seven properties where both lanes have an answer and zero false pet or no-pet facts. The Web Unlocker stays as the fallback because it independently holds seven of those fifteen; it is not retired, it is second.
CHOICE.max_attempts_rationale: 3 is measured, not chosen: Sleep Inn & Suites Milwaukee Airport succeeded on attempt 3 after failing 1 and 2, and Clarion Pointe -- which failed twice under a 2-attempt budget -- succeeded on its first call in the retry. Nothing needed a fourth. SCRAPE_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED is intermittent on this origin, not terminal.
CHOICE.forbidden_rationale: the Browser API was refused 14 times in 15 attempts on Choice and captured nothing. That rule predates this change and nothing measured here touches it.

SONESTA.why: generic walk; part of the MIXED bucket measured at 2/5 in pilot-002

RED_ROOF.why: generic walk. Its identity gate needs the alias mechanism: the brand names this property Cleveland Airport-Middleburg Heights where the record says Red Roof Inn Middleburg Heights

ESA.why: generic walk; policy sits behind a services-and-policies modal that the disclosure pass opens

www.choicehotels.com.why: the same measurement as the CHOICE brand row, pinned to the domain so a property whose brand is unknown takes the same lane

excluded_brands.HYATT: premium domain under the current Bright Data plan, and behind Kasada; excluded on cost, not on capability
excluded_brands.BEST_WESTERN: premium domain under the current Bright Data plan
